_comment: CRITICAL findings that stay in a pinned image because no upstream release removes them yet. One entry per image repository, written by hand: the stacks that use it, why the pin cannot move, the risk, and the findings. Every other CRITICAL is reported by the scan (scripts/ci/trivy-gate.py). The goal is an empty list.

adminer.reason: The newest image was built before Alpine published brotli-libs 1.2.1-r0, and upstream has not rebuilt it. 6.3.0 is the newest Adminer image.
adminer.risk: The library is there for libcurl; Adminer's database connections do not use it (not checked in detail).

akaunting/akaunting.reason: 3.3.0-v (2026-10-27) is the newest Akaunting image, built before Debian's kernel-header fix (6.12.115-2).
akaunting/akaunting.risk: linux-libc-dev holds kernel headers that nothing in the container executes; the running kernel is the host's.

alextselegidis/easyappointments.reason: 1.6.1 (rebuilt 2026-10-22) is the newest release, built before Debian's fixes.
alextselegidis/easyappointments.risk: linux-libc-dev holds kernel headers that nothing in the container executes; the running kernel is the host's. brotli's decoder flaw is reached only if a process decompresses brotli data from a hostile source (in Debian mainly through libcurl); not checked per application.

apache/tika.reason: 3.3.3.0 is the newest Tika 3.x; the fix is in Tika 4, which Paperless-ngx does not support (paperless-ngx/paperless-ngx#14579, closed not planned).
apache/tika.risk: The CXF flaw is an out-of-band XML external entity; whether Tika's REST endpoints reach the affected classes was not checked. Tika sits on an internal network with no outbound route, which blocks the out-of-band leak.

brotandgames/ciao.risk: The Active Storage flaw needs attachments processed by ImageMagick; Ciao stores no attachments. The json gem flaw needs the allow_duplicate_key: false option on user input, not checked. perl-base is the operating system's.

chatwoot/chatwoot.reason: v4.19.1 (2026-10-24) is the newest release; the Active Storage fix needs Rails 8.0.5.2 or later and Chatwoot is on Rails 7.2.
chatwoot/chatwoot.risk: Chatwoot accepts attachments from the public, so the Active Storage flaw (ImageMagick analysis) is potentially reachable; which image processor Chatwoot uses was not checked. net-imap needs unvalidated arguments from inbox settings; zlib reachability not determined.

collabora/code.risk: The DOMPurify flaw applies only with SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES and DOM output modes in the browser-side bundle; whether Collabora uses them was not checked.

defectdojo/defectdojo-django.reason: 3.5.0 (2026-11-02) is the newest release; the -alpine variant would only drop the kernel headers.
defectdojo/defectdojo-django.risk: linux-libc-dev holds kernel headers that nothing in the container executes; the running kernel is the host's. certifi is used for DefectDojo's outbound HTTPS and trusts revoked eMudhra intermediates, which matters only to an on-path attacker holding those keys.

dependencytrack/apiserver.reason: 5.2.1 is the newest release; FreeMarker 2.3.34 comes in through JDBI, whose latest release still depends on it. Upstream: DependencyTrack/dependency-track#7670 (closed, not affected).
dependencytrack/apiserver.risk: FreeMarker is only used by the database layer for SQL templates; upstream states Dependency-Track is not affected.

dependencytrack/frontend.reason: The newest image was built before Alpine published brotli-libs 1.2.1-r0, and upstream has not rebuilt it. 5.2.1 is the newest release.
dependencytrack/frontend.risk: brotli is a dependency of curl and freetype; the nginx serving the static frontend uses neither.

facturascripts/facturascripts.reason: 2026.7 is upstream's stable image (latest); 2026.72, which drops the brotli finding, is published as beta.
facturascripts/facturascripts.risk: linux-libc-dev holds kernel headers that nothing in the container executes; the running kernel is the host's. brotli's decoder flaw is reached only if a process decompresses brotli data from a hostile source (in Debian mainly through libcurl); not checked per application.

frappe/erpnext.reason: v16.53.0 (2026-10-28) is the newest v16 image.
frappe/erpnext.risk: All six findings sit in frappe's node_modules build tooling (loader-utils, shell-quote, the Go runtime inside esbuild), used to build assets, not by the running web, worker or socket.io processes (not verified line by line).

ghcr.io/bluewave-labs/checkmate.risk: Each needs a specific use: user-supplied handlebars templates, a proxy subnet in IPv4-mapped notation, DOMPurify's SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES with DOM output, or the esbuild build step at runtime; Checkmate is not known to make any of them (not checked in its code).

ghcr.io/calnode/calnode.reason: 0.13.0 (2026-11-03) is the newest release; the findings sit in its bundled Litestream binary.
ghcr.io/calnode/calnode.risk: Litestream starts only when LITESTREAM_REPLICA_URL is set, which this stack does not do, and it is a client, not a gRPC server.

ghcr.io/corentinth/it-tools.reason: The last release is from 2024-10-22 on an end-of-life Alpine 3.20; upstream is inactive (CorentinTh/it-tools#1466, #1708). The stack is marked unmaintained.
ghcr.io/corentinth/it-tools.risk: The OpenSSL flaw affects 32-bit systems only; libxml2 is used by nginx's xslt module, which is not loaded by default (not checked); the app is static files run in the browser.

ghcr.io/dfir-iris/iriswebapp_app.reason: v2.4.29 (2026-08-10) is the newest IRIS release and upstream has not rebuilt it.
ghcr.io/dfir-iris/iriswebapp_app.risk: Pillow may be reached through uploaded evidence and avatars; treat it as reachable. PyJWT, libunbound and GnuTLS depend on how IRIS uses them (not checked). Kernel headers are not executed. certifi trusts revoked eMudhra intermediates for outbound TLS.

ghcr.io/dfir-iris/iriswebapp_db.reason: v2.4.29 is the newest IRIS release; its old Alpine base and gosu 1.17 (Go 1.18) were not rebuilt.
ghcr.io/dfir-iris/iriswebapp_db.risk: OpenSSL CVE-2026-31789 is 32-bit only; the Go CVEs are in html/template, net/netip and TLS, which gosu does not use; libxml2 needs schema validation of crafted XML, which PostgreSQL does not do by default (not checked).

ghcr.io/dgtlmoon/changedetection.io.reason: 0.70.1 (2026-11-05) is the newest release; the Rust zip crate sits in the bundled selenium-manager binary.
ghcr.io/dgtlmoon/changedetection.io.risk: selenium-manager only unpacks downloaded browser drivers when Selenium starts a local driver; this stack configures no WebDriver.

ghcr.io/docker-mailserver/docker-mailser.reason: 16.0.1 (2026-09-04) is the newest release; upstream tracks its Debian CVE load in docker-mailserver/docker-mailserver#4822.
ghcr.io/docker-mailserver/docker-mailser.risk: Only OpenDKIM uses libunbound, and this stack runs Rspamd with OpenDKIM, Amavis and SpamAssassin off, so libunbound and the perl mail tools are not reached. The glib flaw is in D-Bus introspection, not plausibly reached by Rspamd (not verified). brotli's decoder flaw is reached only if a process decompresses brotli data from a hostile source (in Debian mainly through libcurl); not checked per application.

ghcr.io/goauthentik/server.reason: 2026.8.5 is the newest release; upstream confirms the finding is not reachable and announces the fix for 2026.8.6 (goauthentik/authentik#27318).
ghcr.io/goauthentik/server.risk: No binary or library in the image links libbrotlidec (checked on the arm64 image).

ghcr.io/gotify/server.reason: 3.1.1 (2026-09-15) is the newest release; the fix is merged upstream (gotify/server#1050) but not released.
ghcr.io/gotify/server.risk: Not reached: the stack uses SQLite (GOTIFY_DATABASE_DIALECT: sqlite3), so the pgx driver is never used.

ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-machine-learni.reason: v3.3.6 is the newest stable Immich release.
ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-machine-learni.risk: The machine-learning service decodes uploaded photos with Pillow, so the Pillow flaws are potentially reachable through any user upload.

ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-server.reason: v3.3.6 (2026-11-04) is the newest stable Immich release; only v3.4.0 release candidates follow.
ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-server.risk: handlebars needs attacker-controlled templates (Immich's are admin-set); tar is a decompression denial of service through archive handling (not checked); proxy-addr matters only for IPv4-mapped IPv6 trusted-proxy entries; brotli not determined.

ghcr.io/immich-app/postgres.reason: VectorChord 1.1.1 is the newest release; the 14-, 16-, 17- and 18-vectorchord1.1.1 images are all built on the same Debian 12 base with perl 5.36.0-7+deb12u3 and gosu built with Go 1.24.6.
ghcr.io/immich-app/postgres.risk: PostgreSQL does not run Perl on user data; CVE-2026-8376 affects 32-bit builds only. gosu opens no TLS connection. Reachable only if something in the container runs Perl on untrusted input (not checked).

ghcr.io/intuitem/ciso-assistant-communit.reason: v4.2.1 (2026-11-01) is the newest release, built before Debian's kernel-header fix.
ghcr.io/intuitem/ciso-assistant-communit.risk: linux-libc-dev holds kernel headers that nothing in the container executes; the running kernel is the host's.

ghcr.io/obot-platform/obot.risk: Obot makes outbound TLS calls and its trust store still includes revoked eMudhra intermediates, which matters only to an on-path attacker holding those keys. Whether brotli decoding is used was not checked.

ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui.reason: v0.13.0 (2026-11-03) is the newest release and upstream's development branch still pins the vulnerable versions.
ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui.risk: Authlib matters if OAuth/OIDC login is configured; PyJWT only where HMAC and public-key algorithms are mixed; sentence-transformers runs code from a model directory an attacker can write to; unstructured is an SSRF when it fetches a URL. Reachability of each not checked.

ghcr.io/psf/httpbin.reason: 0.10.4 (2026-06-16) is the newest release and has not been rebuilt.
ghcr.io/psf/httpbin.risk: httpbin only compresses with brotli, while the flaw is in the decoder; perl is not used by the app.

ghcr.io/requarks/wiki.reason: 3.1.0 (2026-11-05) is the newest release, built before Debian's kernel-header fix.
ghcr.io/requarks/wiki.risk: linux-libc-dev holds kernel headers that nothing in the container executes; the running kernel is the host's.

ghcr.io/rubennati/cal.diy.reason: This project's own build of the Cal.diy fork, on Next.js 16.2.3 and Debian 12. The fixes need a rebuild of the fork on Next.js 16.4.1 or later and a current base image; that rebuild is planned and not done.
ghcr.io/rubennati/cal.diy.risk: Next.js, Sentry and the Node.js packages sit in the web application's request path and count as reachable; whether each advisory applies to Cal.diy's use has not been checked. The Debian packages and kernel headers are not on that path. Shipped default is access-vpn.

ghcr.io/rubennati/cert-ops-tool.reason: This project's own build on Alpine; the fixes need a rebuild on a current Alpine base, which is planned and not done.
ghcr.io/rubennati/cert-ops-tool.risk: No published port and no inbound connections; the container only connects out to the ACME CA and the Cloudflare API. openssl is on that path; whether the scripts use socat or bind-tools has not been checked.

ghcr.io/shlinkio/shlink.reason: The newest image was built before Alpine published brotli-libs 1.2.1-r0, and upstream has not rebuilt it. 5.1.8 is the newest release.
ghcr.io/shlinkio/shlink.risk: The library backs PHP's curl, which Shlink uses when it fetches remote pages such as a long URL's title, so a hostile site could in principle reach it (not checked).

ghcr.io/shlinkio/shlink-web-client.reason: The newest image was built before Alpine published brotli-libs 1.2.1-r0, and upstream has not rebuilt it. 4.9.0 is the newest release.
ghcr.io/shlinkio/shlink-web-client.risk: brotli is a dependency of curl and freetype, which the nginx serving the static client does not use.

ghcr.io/windmill-labs/windmill.reason: 1.862.0 (2026-11-04) is the newest release, built before Debian's kernel-header fix.
ghcr.io/windmill-labs/windmill.risk: linux-libc-dev holds kernel headers that nothing in the container executes; the running kernel is the host's.

ghost.reason: 6.75.0-alpine is the newest 6.x release. gosu 1.19 in the official image is built with Go 1.24.6; gosu 1.20 exists (2026-10-25) but the official Dockerfile still pins 1.19 and the current digest is the one scanned. Upstream: docker-library/mysql#1135 (closed, govulncheck finds no reachable symbol), docker-library/mongo#760 (open).
ghost.risk: The flaw is in Go's crypto/tls session resumption. gosu only drops privileges at container start and opens no TLS connection, so the code is not reached.

greenmail/standalone.reason: 2.1.15 is the newest release and has not been rebuilt.
greenmail/standalone.risk: Only the font library depends on brotli, and GreenMail renders no fonts.

hemmeligapp/hemmelig.reason: The upstream project is archived (HemmeligOrg/Hemmelig.app, last release v7.6.1 of 2026-09-25); no fixed release will follow. The stack is marked unmaintained.
hemmeligapp/hemmelig.risk: The better-auth flaw needs the Magic Link plugin, which Hemmelig does not load; npm's tar does not run in the container; perl and GnuTLS reachability not checked.

heyform/community-edition.reason: v3.0.6 (2026-11-01) is the newest HeyForm release.
heyform/community-edition.risk: Most findings belong to build and test tools in node_modules (vitest, tinypool, esbuild, shell-quote, tar) that the running server does not use; proxy-addr does not apply because the stack trusts the proxy by hop count (TRUST_PROXY=1). Whether handlebars, form-data and sha.js are reached was not checked.

invoiceninja/invoiceninja-debian.reason: 5.13.53 (2026-11-02) is the newest release and its digest is unchanged since the scan; the Debian kernel-header fix (6.12.115-2) is newer than the build.
invoiceninja/invoiceninja-debian.risk: linux-libc-dev holds kernel headers that nothing in the container runs; the running kernel is the host's.

jhumanj/opnform-api.reason: The newest image was built before Alpine published brotli-libs 1.2.1-r0, and upstream has not rebuilt it. 2.8.4 is the newest OpnForm release.
jhumanj/opnform-api.risk: The library backs PHP's curl, which OpnForm uses for outbound requests such as webhooks, so a hostile endpoint answering with brotli could in principle reach the decoder (not checked).

jumpserver/jms_all.reason: v5.1.1 (2026-10-20) is the newest JumpServer release; upstream has not rebuilt it with the fixed Tomcat, Spring, Netty, Pillow and Debian packages.
jumpserver/jms_all.risk: Tomcat, Spring Web MVC and Pillow are in the request path of the bundled web components and count as reachable for anyone who reaches the UI. certifi and the JDK trust revoked eMudhra intermediates, which matters only to an on-path attacker holding those keys. Shipped default is access-vpn.

kimai/kimai2.risk: brotli's decoder flaw is reached only if a process decompresses brotli data from a hostile source (in Debian mainly through libcurl); not checked per application.

kopia/kopia.reason: v0.23.1 (2026-06-16) is the newest stable release; newer tags are dated nightlies.
kopia/kopia.risk: Both findings sit in the bundled rclone binary, which Kopia runs only for an rclone storage backend; this stack uses a filesystem repository.

langgenius/dify-sandbox.risk: The sandbox runs user code in Python and Node, not Perl; perl-base is the Debian base's. anyio and certifi affect outbound TLS verification from sandboxed code, which reaches the network only through the stack's squid proxy.

leantime/leantime.risk: The jmespath flaw needs its opt-in compiler, off by default. brotli's decoder flaw is reached only if a process decompresses brotli data from a hostile source (in Debian mainly through libcurl); not checked per application.

listmonk/listmonk.reason: v6.2.0 (2026-06-26) is the newest stable release; v7 is beta (knadh/listmonk#3339).
listmonk/listmonk.risk: The flaw is in Echo's Proxy middleware; a code search found no use of it in listmonk, so it is likely not reached (code search only).

louislam/uptime-kuma.reason: 2.5.9 (2026-10-31) is the newest release and has not been rebuilt; the -slim variant drops only the Chromium findings and also drops Real Browser monitors and the embedded MariaDB.
louislam/uptime-kuma.risk: Chromium runs only for Real Browser monitors and loads the monitored page; protobufjs only for gRPC monitors with an untrusted definition; the Go runtime sits in the healthcheck helper; tar and brotli are not reached in normal use.

lscr.io/linuxserver/unifi-network-applic.reason: 10.6.109 (ls153, 2026-11-03) is the newest UniFi Network Application release; the vulnerable Tomcat, Spring and Bouncy Castle jars ship inside Ubiquiti's application, which the image packager cannot replace.
lscr.io/linuxserver/unifi-network-applic.risk: Tomcat serves the controller's web interface and API, so its connector flaws are reachable on that port; whether the authenticator or XsltView items apply was not checked. Keep the controller off the public internet.

makeplane/plane-backend.reason: v1.4.3 is the newest stable Plane release.
makeplane/plane-backend.risk: PyJWT's flaw applies when an application accepts mixed key types; whether Plane's token handling does has not been checked.

makeplane/plane-live.reason: v1.4.3 (2026-10-28) is the newest stable Plane release; only release candidates follow.
makeplane/plane-live.risk: storybook and tinypool are development and test tools in node_modules that the server does not run. proxy-addr matters only for trusted-proxy entries in IPv4-mapped IPv6 form (not checked).

makeplane/plane-proxy.reason: v1.4.3 is the newest stable Plane release; upstream has not rebuilt its Alpine base.
makeplane/plane-proxy.risk: Brotli's decoder flaw needs untrusted brotli input to be decompressed; a reverse proxy normally compresses responses, but whether this one uses the library was not checked.

makeplane/plane-space.reason: v1.4.3 (2026-10-28) is the newest stable Plane release; only release candidates follow.
makeplane/plane-space.risk: Same as plane-live: storybook and tinypool are not run; proxy-addr matters only for IPv4-mapped IPv6 trusted-proxy entries.

mariadb.reason: Seafile 13 names mariadb:10.11; every newer MariaDB line (11.4, 11.8, 12.3) carries the same gosu build. gosu 1.19 in the official image is built with Go 1.24.6; gosu 1.20 exists (2026-10-25) but the official Dockerfile still pins 1.19 and the current digest is the one scanned. Upstream: docker-library/mysql#1135 (closed, govulncheck finds no reachable symbol), docker-library/mongo#760 (open).
mariadb.risk: The flaw is in Go's crypto/tls session resumption. gosu only drops privileges at container start and opens no TLS connection, so the code is not reached.

mongo.reason: 8.0 resolves to 8.0.34, the newest 8.0 patch. gosu 1.19 in the official image is built with Go 1.24.6; gosu 1.20 exists (2026-10-25) but the official Dockerfile still pins 1.19 and the current digest is the one scanned. Upstream: docker-library/mysql#1135 (closed, govulncheck finds no reachable symbol), docker-library/mongo#760 (open).
mongo.risk: The flaw is in Go's crypto/tls session resumption. gosu only drops privileges at container start and opens no TLS connection, so the code is not reached.

monica.reason: 4.1.2 (2024-05-04) is the newest stable Monica release; the official 5.0 images are 5.0.0-beta.5 and would still carry the Laravel finding. The stack is marked as not current.
monica.risk: Monica's api guard uses Passport, not Laravel's TokenGuard, so the Laravel flaw is not reached; the jmespath flaw needs the opt-in compiler; symfony/process affects Windows only. The application itself is no longer actively released.

mysql.reason: 8.4 is the current LTS build (2026-11-03) and 9.7.4 carries the same two findings. gosu 1.19 in the official image is built with Go 1.24.6; gosu 1.20 exists (2026-10-25) but the official Dockerfile still pins 1.19 and the current digest is the one scanned. Upstream: docker-library/mysql#1135 (closed, govulncheck finds no reachable symbol), docker-library/mongo#760 (open). certifi 2026.2.25 is bundled with MySQL Shell's Python.
mysql.risk: The flaw is in Go's crypto/tls session resumption. gosu only drops privileges at container start and opens no TLS connection, so the code is not reached. certifi trusts distrusted emSign intermediates only for MySQL Shell's outbound TLS; the database server does not use it and neither stack runs mysqlsh.

n8nio/n8n.reason: The newest image was built before Alpine published brotli-libs 1.2.1-r0, and upstream has not rebuilt it. 2.46.6 is the newest stable n8n release; 2.47 is a pre-release.
n8nio/n8n.risk: Node.js, which makes n8n's own HTTP requests, has its own brotli; the Alpine library serves curl and freetype, so a workflow running curl against an untrusted server could reach it (not checked).

openproject/openproject.reason: 17.9.6 (2026-10-30) is the newest release; 18.0 is still a release candidate.
openproject/openproject.risk: The Active Storage flaw needs attachments analysed with ImageMagick and the json flaw needs allow_duplicate_key: false on user input; whether OpenProject reaches either was not checked.

opensign/opensign.reason: Upstream publishes only rolling main/staging builds; the pinned digest is the current main (2026-11-02), which already contains v3.1.0, and staging carries the same findings. Both images are built FROM node:22.14.0, an early-2025 Debian 12 base (upstream issue OpenSignLabs/OpenSign#2323).
opensign/opensign.risk: Not determined per package. ImageMagick, libxml2 and glib come with the full Node base image; whether OpenSign calls them has not been checked. linux-libc-dev is kernel headers that nothing runs. Keep OpenSign behind authentication and limit who can upload.

opensign/opensignserver.reason: Same as opensign/opensign: rolling main is the newest build, on the node:22.14.0 base (OpenSignLabs/OpenSign#2323).
opensign/opensignserver.risk: The server converts uploaded documents, so parser flaws in its Debian packages are plausibly reachable; proxy-addr matters only with a subnet trust-proxy setting. Not determined per package.

owasp/threat-dragon.risk: The server trusts every proxy hop already (trust proxy true), so the proxy-addr subnet flaw adds nothing; the npm CLI does not run in the container.

pgautoupgrade/pgautoupgrade.reason: Every current official image of this line ships gosu 1.19 (or 1.20) built with Go 1.24.6, and the gosu maintainer has not rebuilt it with a fixed Go (tianon/gosu#176); no tag removes the finding.
pgautoupgrade/pgautoupgrade.risk: The flaw is in Go's crypto/tls session resumption. gosu only drops root privileges at container start and opens no TLS connection, so the code is not reached.

pgvector/pgvector.reason: Every current official image of this line ships gosu 1.19 (or 1.20) built with Go 1.24.6, and the gosu maintainer has not rebuilt it with a fixed Go (tianon/gosu#176); no tag removes the finding.
pgvector/pgvector.risk: The flaw is in Go's crypto/tls session resumption. gosu only drops root privileges at container start and opens no TLS connection, so the code is not reached.

photoview/photoview.reason: 2.4.0 (2024-06-23) is the newest release; the image is rebuilt but still compiled with Go 1.19.
photoview/photoview.risk: pgx is not used (MariaDB). The Go 1.19 standard library is the server's runtime and in the request path; which affected functions Photoview calls was not checked. The stack ships access-public.

postgres.reason: Every current official image of this line ships gosu 1.19 (or 1.20) built with Go 1.24.6, and the gosu maintainer has not rebuilt it with a fixed Go (tianon/gosu#176); no tag removes the finding.
postgres.risk: The flaw is in Go's crypto/tls session resumption. gosu only drops root privileges at container start and opens no TLS connection, so the code is not reached. The Alpine OpenSSL finding some older tags carried is gone at the current pins.

rabbitmq.reason: The 3.x line ends at 3.13.7 and Docker Hub no longer rebuilds it; only 4.x is rebuilt, and neither IRIS nor Plane documents RabbitMQ 4 support.
rabbitmq.risk: CVE-2026-31789 (OpenSSL) is a heap overflow on 32-bit platforms only; these images are amd64/arm64. The broker sits on the internal network.

seafileltd/sdoc-server.reason: 2.0.11 is the newest stable tag of the 2.0 line Seafile 13 uses; 2.0.12 exists only as -testing and 3.0 belongs to Seafile 14.
seafileltd/sdoc-server.risk: PyJWT's flaw concerns asymmetric-key tokens; Seafile signs with a shared secret, so the path is likely unused (not verified in code). proxy-addr can let a client spoof its logged IP address with a subnet trust-proxy setting.

seafileltd/seafile-ai.reason: 13.0.10 is the newest image for Seafile 13; the 14.0 line belongs to Seafile 14, which upstream still labels beta.
seafileltd/seafile-ai.risk: LiteLLM authentication bypasses and Pillow decoding overflows are reachable once the AI service runs. It is optional and off by default (not in COMPOSE_FILE, ENABLE_SEAFILE_AI=false).

seafileltd/thumbnail-server.reason: 13.0.29 is the newest Seafile 13 tag; 14.0 belongs to Seafile 14.
seafileltd/thumbnail-server.risk: PyJWT's flaw concerns asymmetric-key tokens; Seafile signs with a shared secret, so the path is likely unused (not verified in code).

smallstep/step-ca.reason: 0.30.2 (2026-03-23) is the newest release; related upstream issues smallstep/certificates#2730 and #2500.
smallstep/step-ca.risk: pgx sits in the step CLI and this stack uses the badger database, so it is not reached. The OpenSSL flaw affects 32-bit systems only. The CA does not use brotli.

thinkst/opencanary.reason: 0.9.10 (2026-09-21) is the newest release and has not been rebuilt.
thinkst/opencanary.risk: The honeypot listeners are Python/Twisted services; ImageMagick, perl, brotli and the uv tool come from the base image and are not on that path (uv not run by the service, not verified). certifi matters only for outbound HTTPS alerting.

uroni/urbackup-server.reason: The 2.5.x digest (2.5.38, 2026-08-30) has not been rebuilt by upstream.
uroni/urbackup-server.risk: Neither package is part of the backup protocol. brotli's decoder flaw is reached only if a process decompresses brotli data from a hostile source (in Debian mainly through libcurl); not checked per application. perl-base is the operating system's.

unscanned.quay.io/minio/minio: MinIO withdrew its public container images: quay.io answers UNAUTHORIZED, the Docker Hub repository is gone, and minio/minio was archived on GitHub on 2026-04-24. Not transient and not a rate limit — there is no public source left to scan. business/plane and monitoring/langfuse stop at it, which both READMEs state; replacing it with a versioned S3-compatible store is an open item in .ai/tasks.md.
